topic.name: Finding the Common Difference of an Arithmetic Sequence

question.text: Find the common difference of an arithmetic sequence if its fourth and fifth terms are $1$ and $7$, respectively.
question.explanation:
The first thing to note is that the terms are increasing, and therefore we expect the common difference $d$ to be positive.

Since the two terms are consecutive, we can find the common difference by subtracting $a_{4}$ from $a_{5}\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} d&=a_5-a_4 \\[3pt] &=7-1 \\[3pt] &=6 \end{align*}

Therefore, the common difference is $d=6.$

example.title: Finding the Common Difference Given Two Consecutive Terms

question.text: An arithmetic sequence has $a_{9}=9$ and $a_{22}=178.$ What is the common difference of the sequence?
question.explanation:
The first thing to note is that the terms are increasing, and therefore we expect $d$ to be positive.

We are given the terms

\[ a_{9} = 9, \quad a_{22} = 178. \]

To find $d,$ we apply the formula with $n=22$ and $m=9\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} d &= \frac{a_n-a_m}{n-m} \\[5pt] &= \frac{a_{22}-a_{9}}{22-9} \\[5pt] &= \frac{178-9}{22-9} \\[5pt] &= \frac{169}{13} \\[5pt] &=13 \end{align*}

Therefore, the common difference is $d=13.$

example.title: Finding the Common Difference Given Two Non-Consecutive Terms

question.text: Find the common difference of an arithmetic sequence if its seventh and twenty-second terms are $126$ and $-9$, respectively.
question.explanation:
The first thing to note is that the terms are decreasing, and therefore we expect $d$ to be negative.

We are given the terms

\[ a_7 = 126, \quad a_{22} = -9. \]

So, to find $d,$ we apply the formula with $n=22$ and $m=7\mathbin{:}$ \[ \begin{align} d &= \frac{a_n-a_m}{n-m} \\[5pt] &= \frac{a_{22}-a_{7}}{22-7} \\[5pt] &= \frac{(-9) - 126}{22-7} \\[5pt] &= \frac{-135}{15}\\[5pt] &=-9 \end{align} \]

Therefore, the common difference is $d=-9.$
